records.title: Human Cytochrome P450 Cancer-Related Metabolic Activities and Gene Polymorphisms: A Review.
records.abstract_excerpt:
Background

Cytochromes P450 (CYPs) are heme-containing oxidoreductase enzymes with mono-oxygenase activity. Human CYPs catalyze the oxidation of a great variety of chemicals, including xenobiotics, steroid hormones, vitamins, bile acids, procarcinogens, and drugs.

Findings

records.abstract_excerpt:
Background

Exposure to chemical mixtures inherent in air pollution, has been shown to be associated with the risk of breast and lung cancers. assistant_message.content:
**Revised Narrative**

The most strongly enriched pathway is **Biological oxidations (Reactome R-HSA-211859)** with a fold-enrichment of 128.5, reflecting the overwhelming representation of xenobiotic-metabolizing enzymes across the input list. Seven of the nine metabolites map to this pathway, spanning the full arc of drug metabolism: Phase I oxidations (bromide, coumarin, methimazole, N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl), Phase II conjugation (benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide, N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl, glutathione, beta-mercaptoethanol), and direct xenobiotic clearance (bromide). A second, equally significant hit is **Phase II - Conjugation of compounds (R-HSA-156580)**, with benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (C14853) and N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl (C20319) as dense connectors — both are annotated in multiple reactions involving glutathione, sulfate, and glucuronide transferases.

**Key driver metabolites.** The most functionally central compounds are benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (C14853), N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl (C20319), and glutathione (C00051). Benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide is the ultimate carcinogenic diol-epoxide metabolite of benzo[a]pyrene; literature reports that GSH S-transferases (GSTs) mediate its conjugation with glutathione to mitigate adduct formation (PMID 41336283). N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl similarly represents the N-hydroxylated activation product of 4-aminobiphenyl, an aromatic amine carcinogen, and is confirmed as a member of Phase II conjugation pathways. Glutathione itself is the terminal nucleophile in these conjugation reactions. Pantothenic acid (C00864) was identified as differentially abundant in the input list and maps to Biological oxidations.

**Biological significance.** The coordinated enrichment across Biological oxidations and Phase II - Conjugation of compounds points to xenobiotic stress responses and active detoxification processing as the dominant biological perturbation in the treatment group. The absence of a short KEGG reaction path between the carcinogen epoxides and glutathione reflects the exogenous, annotation-driven nature of these relationships rather than a gap in detoxification capacity.

**Limitations.** CYP1A1/1B1 enzyme involvement is inferred from literature rather than from the enrichment output. Direct database membership of C14853 in Reactome conjugation pathways is not confirmed in RaMP/KEGG; literature evidence (PMID 41336283) provides indirect support. Additional wet-lab or transcriptomic data would strengthen the mechanistic interpretation.
